title: Tag every horizon boundary along an opened soil core
instruction: This soil core lies open in the black tray. Stand one white tag upright on the tray right next to the core at each place where one soil layer meets the next, one tag per boundary. Then let go and lift the grippers clear.
context: Before a soil core is sampled, a soil scientist or environmental technician logs it. They find each boundary between horizons by its colour change, mark it, and record its depth. Samples are then taken within one layer, never across a boundary. The work is done by soil scientists, environmental science and protection technicians and geoscientists (O*NET 19-1013, 19-4042, 19-2042), following the USDA NRCS Field Book for Describing and Sampling Soils and ASTM D5434 (field logging of subsurface explorations). A supervisor checks a logged core the way this task is scored: a ruler from each mark to the colour change.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Depth down the core is measured from its top end: depth = 28.0 cm - y. Three kinds of thing are on the table. (1) Core tray: a flat matte black rigid plastic board, 180 mm along x, 720 mm along y and 6 mm thick, fixed to the table, spanning x 32.0 to 50.0 cm and y +31.0 to -41.0 cm. (2) Soil core: an opened core, a straight flat-topped band 50 mm wide (x 38.5 to 43.5 cm) and 30 mm tall, fixed, lying on the tray (its top 36 mm above the table) and running along y from its top end (the ground surface) at y +28.0 cm to 560 mm deep at y -28.0 cm. The tray reaches 30 mm beyond the core's top end and 130 mm beyond its bottom end. The core is painted in five matte horizons, top down: A 0-46 mm deep, dark brown (sRGB 0.36, 0.25, 0.16); E 46-173 mm, light brownish grey (0.75, 0.70, 0.60); Bt 173-314 mm, reddish brown (0.60, 0.30, 0.18); BC 314-434 mm, yellowish brown (0.78, 0.60, 0.32); C 434-560 mm, olive grey (0.50, 0.52, 0.42). The four boundaries are therefore 46, 173, 314 and 434 mm deep (y +23.4, +10.7, -3.4 and -15.4 cm). In simulation the core is seven fixed boxes that abut exactly with equal tops: Bt and BC are each two boxes of one colour, joined at 245 and 374 mm deep, so a joint between boxes is not a sign of a boundary. A real build is one continuous 560 x 50 x 30 mm wooden or printed bar painted in the five bands and taped to the tray. (3) Four depth tags: white rigid plastic cylinders (for example cut from 20 mm white nylon rod), 20 mm across and 40 mm tall, 15 g each, with flat ends (either end may be down), standing upright on the table in a pair at each end of the tray, as on a long logging bench with a box of tags kept at each end: x 20.0 cm, y +40.0 cm; x 28.0 cm, y +40.0 cm; x 20.0 cm, y -40.0 cm; and x 28.0 cm, y -40.0 cm. The pair at y +40 cm is beyond the right arm's reach and the pair at y -40 cm beyond the left arm's. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The scorer reads the four tags every control step (20 Hz) and, from the embodiment's state, each gripper's pad-tip point (13 mm past its tool point, midway between the finger tips) and how far it is open. A tag is 'placed' when all of these hold: (a) upright: its axis within 10 degrees of vertical, either end down; (b) on the tray: its lowest point within 3 mm of the tray's top (3 to 9 mm above the table), so not on the core, on another tag or on the table; (c) still: its centre's path over the last 0.5 s (10 control steps) is under 3 mm; (d) beside the core: its centre is outside the core and at most 45 mm from the core's nearer long edge (x 34.0 to 38.5 cm, or 43.5 to 48.0 cm; a tag pressed against the core counts); (e) let go and clear: no gripper's pad-tip point is lower than 10 mm above the tag's top while the tag's axis is within that gripper's finger reach horizontally. The gripper's yaw is not read, so the reach is the widest over every yaw: hypot(half the finger gap + 10 mm, 20 mm) + 15 mm, which is 75 mm fully open, 43 mm closed on a tag and 37 mm fully closed, so a finger touching or propping the tag from any side counts as holding it. A boundary is 'tagged' when a placed tag's centre is within 10 mm of it along the core (in y). The boundaries are at least 120 mm apart, so one tag can tag at most one boundary, and each boundary counts once however many tags are near it. Score = 0.25 x the number of boundaries tagged: 1.0 all four; 0.75 three; 0.5 two; 0.25 one; 0 none (for example every tag still at its start, lying down, stacked on another tag, standing on the core, still held, or more than 10 mm from every boundary). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. The trial ends early once all four boundaries have stayed tagged for 1 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. On a step where the grippers cannot be read, rule (e) is taken as met. Tags put down without looking at the colours: the points dividing the core or the tray into 2 to 6 equal parts, the centres of 1 to 4 equal parts, 2 to 5 points spread from end to end, a tag every 10 or 20 cm from either end of the core or from the tray's bottom end, and the ends are all at least 13 mm from every boundary (0). The centres of 5 equal parts of the core or the tray, or a tag every 10 or 20 cm from the tray's top end, tag one boundary (0.25), or, for 5-part centres placed a few mm off, two (0.5). Denser spreads (6 to 12 parts, every 5 cm) reach at most two boundaries (0.5). In a real trial, after the arms have withdrawn, take a top photo with a ruler laid along the core and measure from each standing tag's centre to the nearest colour change.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, one friction value for everything. Horizons are crisp colour changes between rigid painted blocks; real boundaries can be gradual or wavy and are also judged by texture and feel, which the simulator does not show. The core is a flat-topped bar, not a half-round core in a cut liner, and the tags stand beside it instead of nails pushed into the soil. Depths are not written down; only the marks are scored. The grippers are read only to check that each tag was let go.
reset_notes: Stand the four tags back upright on the table at x 20.0 cm, y +40.0 cm; x 28.0 cm, y +40.0 cm; x 20.0 cm, y -40.0 cm; and x 28.0 cm, y -40.0 cm. The tray and the core stay fixed (on a real rig the core bar is taped to the tray). Nothing is consumed.
